name: Crayon
summary: A picture-book page drawn live in wax crayon on toothy paper: indigo outlines that boil on twos, zig-zag colouring that skips over the paper's tooth, hand-lettered words, and one watercolour wash that reveals what white crayon was hiding.

palette.use: the warm off-white page; also the ragged knock-out patches behind words
indigo: every outline and every hand-lettered word (outlines are never black)
indigo at light pressure: kickers and small notes (proposed)
the paper's shadow side: tooth emboss and the warm vignette (proposed)
sky crayon: blue light, the thing the film is about
yellow crayon: the sun and sunlight
orange crayon: sun rays, warm accents
red crayon: red light, small dots
pink crayon: cheeks, a blush scribble
ochre crayon: the air molecule, sand
white crayon reserved for resist: nearly invisible until the wash passes
the one watercolour (cerulean), multiplied over the page at the wash density; never paints characters (proposed hex)

type.emphasis: colour, not type: a word lettered in a crayon colour, scribbled under, or revealed by the wash

motion.exit: none: drawings leave by a page turn or by being coloured over, never by fading

banned: cute vector art with a crayon filter: the look comes from wax catching the paper's tooth
black outlines: outlines are one dark colour (indigo here)
more than about a dozen crayons, or more than one watercolour per film
the wash painting a character: characters keep the paper white
dark subtitle boxes: words sit on ragged patches of blank paper
fading crayon or titles in or out: things are drawn on and leave by a page turn or being coloured over
a screen-fixed paper tooth: the tooth belongs to the page
light-pressure colour under a wash (it goes muddy): use pressure 0.8 or more, or cross-hatch
a whiteboard, chalkboard or watercolour-painting look: no markers, no slate, the wash is a guest
